title: Pop Application: Disco, Punk & Hip-Hop

concepts.def: Late 70s rebellion: fast, raw, DIY (Sex Pistols 1976).
1970s NYC genre: MCing, DJing, sampling, breakbeats.
Kick drum on every crotchet beat — disco/EDM.
Using a snippet of existing audio in a new track.
Disc jockey — plays records and manipulates them live.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Disco ruled the late 1970s — Donna Summer, Bee Gees, Chic. Key features: four-on-the-floor kick drum, syncopated bass, lush string sections, hi-hats on the off-beats and falsetto vocals.

Tempo sits around 110–130 BPM — built for dancing all night.

Punk exploded in 1976 with the Sex Pistols and The Clash. Songs were under 3 minutes, fast (180+ BPM), with shouted vocals, distorted guitars and basic three-chord structures.

The DIY ethos rejected music-industry polish — anyone could form a band, record cheaply and release their own music.

walkthroughs.h2: From the Bronx to the world
walkthroughs.body_html:
Hip-hop began in the 1970s Bronx — DJ Kool Herc looped 'breaks' from funk records so MCs could rap over them. Four elements: MCing, DJing, breakdancing, graffiti.

Sampling became central — chopping up old records to create new beats (e.g. The Sugarhill Gang's Rapper's Delight, 1979).
